title: Recall division facts as the inverse of multiplication facts

lesson.title: Flip It! Division Facts Hide Inside Multiplication

steps.say: You already know your multiplication facts for twos, threes, fours, fives and tens — and today we use them to make division super fast. When you see a division fact, you do not have to count it out. You just flip a multiplication fact you already know.

Here are twenty maple cookies packed into four bags, five cookies in each bag. Four times five is twenty. Now look at the very same picture and ask a division question: twenty cookies shared into bags of five — how many bags? Four bags. Same picture, same three numbers, just read a different way.

So here is the trick. When you see a division question, turn it into a missing number multiplication question. For twenty-four divided by four, whisper to yourself: four times what equals twenty-four? Run through your fours — four, eight, twelve, sixteen, twenty, twenty-four. That is six fours. So twenty-four divided by four is six.

Careful with one slip lots of kids make. They think of the fact four times six equals twenty-four, then they say the answer is twenty-four. But twenty-four is the total — it is the number you started with, so it cannot be the answer. The answer is the missing piece, the number of groups. Six. Always grab the number that was hiding, not the big total.

visual.caption: 24 is the whole pile; 6 is the answer we were missing

steps.say: Let's check it the easy way. Multiply your answer back: six times four is twenty-four. It matches the number you started with, so you know you are right. Multiplication and division are best friends — one undoes the other.
So remember: division is just multiplication wearing a different hat. Ask what times this gives me that, and the answer pops right out.

lesson.answer: To divide, ask 'what times this equals that?' — the missing factor is your answer.

practice.question: Hockey card packs cost five dollars each at the corner store. Liam spends thirty-five dollars altogether. Work out thirty-five divided by five by asking yourself: five times what number equals thirty-five? How many packs did Liam buy? (Try drawing groups of five dots if it helps.)
practice.answer: Seven packs. Five times seven equals thirty-five, so thirty-five divided by five is seven. Check it: seven times five is thirty-five.
